body.p: **Θα** is invariable and unstressed. It always stands directly before the verb (weak pronouns go between them).

head: θα +
Meaning
Example
rows: Θα σε περιμένω. I'll be waiting for you.
Θα σε δω αύριο. I'll see you tomorrow.
Θα ήθελα έναν καφέ. I'd like a coffee.
Θα είχα έρθει. I would have come.
Θα έχω φύγει. I'll have left.
Θα είναι εννιά. It must be nine.

ex.en: Will you bring it to me?

body.p: Word order is fixed: **(δεν) θα (weak pronouns) verb**. **Θα** never takes a weak pronoun before it, and nothing else can come between θα and the verb except weak pronouns.
**Historically**, θα comes from **θέλω να** "I want to" → θε να → θα, a path also seen in English "will".
Greek has three negators, and the choice is grammatical.

head: Negator
Where
Example
rows: with να, ας, commands, wishes, purpose, the gerund
alone ("no"), and to negate a word or phrase
Όχι, ευχαριστώ. Θέλω καφέ, όχι τσάι.

ex.en: I want him not to come.

body.p: The final **-ν** of **δεν** and **μην** follows the same rule as **την** (kept before vowels and κ, π, τ, ξ, ψ, γκ, μπ, ντ, τσ, τζ): **δεν έχω, δεν ξέρω, δε θέλω** (written δεν θέλω too: many writers now always keep the ν of δεν), **μην ανησυχείς, μη φύγεις**.

**Double negation** is the norm: **Δεν είδα κανέναν** "I didn't see anyone", **Δεν θέλω τίποτα** "I don't want anything", **Δεν πάω πουθενά** "I'm not going anywhere", **Δεν τον έχω δει ποτέ** "I've never seen him".

check.why: A word or phrase is negated with όχι.

sections.title: Yes and no: ναι, όχι, μάλιστα, μπα

body.p: **Ναι** "yes", **όχι** "no". **Μάλιστα** is a polite or formal "yes, certainly, indeed" (also "I see" when listening), and **μπα** is a casual "nah, no way".

ex.en: Would you like anything else? No, thank you.
Will you come? Nah, I don't think so.

body.tip: The Greek **ναι** sounds like English "nay", and the head gesture for "no" is an upward nod with raised eyebrows (often with a click of the tongue, **τσκ**). A downward tilt of the head means yes.

body.p: **Answering negative questions**: **ναι** agrees with the facts as stated positively, as in English: **Δεν ήρθε; Όχι, δεν ήρθε** "Didn't he come? No, he didn't" / **Ναι, ήρθε** "Yes, he did".
**Να** marks the subjunctive. It is the most frequent particle after και and the article, because it replaces the English infinitive.

head: Use
Example
English
rows: Shall we go to the cinema?

body.p: Word order: **να (μη) (weak pronouns) verb**: **να μην του το πεις** "don't tell it to him".

check.why: A suggestion in question form: να πάμε; (Ας πάμε! is "let's go!".)

body.p: **Ας** + subjunctive-type form means "let (me, us, him)". It expresses suggestions, permission, indifference and regret.

head: Use
Example
English
rows: Let him come if he wants.
Ας είναι και ακριβό, θα το πάρω.
Even if it's expensive, I'll take it.

ex.en: Let's not talk about it any more.
Let him say what he likes.

body.p: **Άσε, άσ' το, άσε να** (from αφήνω) is the everyday "let, leave it": **Άσε με να σου εξηγήσω** "Let me explain"; **Άσ' το!** "Forget it!", **Άσε!** "Don't even ask!"

check.q: Άσε! (alone, in reply to "How was your day?") means:
check.why: Άσε! as an exclamation: "Don't even ask".

sections.title: Pointing να: "there is!, here it is!"

body.p: A different **να**, the deictic (pointing) particle, means "here is, there is, look!". It is stressed and often followed by a special weak pronoun or a noun in the nominative.

head: Pronoun forms after deictic να
rows: There they are! (neut.) / Look what happened!

ex.en: There you go! (said when something predictable happens)

body.p: The forms **τος, τοι, τες** occur only after deictic να and after **πού 'ναι** in speech: **Πού 'ν' τος;** "Where is he?"

sections.title: Urging and encouraging: για, έλα, άντε, για να δούμε

body.p: **Για** + imperative (hortatory για) urges: "come on, just". **Έλα** "come on" (imperative of έρχομαι), **άντε** "go on, come on", **για να δούμε** "let's see".

ex.en: Come on, tell me what happened.

body.p: **Έλα** also answers the phone ("Hello? / Yes?") among friends, and expresses surprise or disbelief: **Έλα! Αλήθεια;** "No way! Really?"

**Άντε** has many tones: impatience (**Άντε, άργησες!** "Come on, you're late!"), wishes (**Άντε, και στα δικά σου!** "Here's to yours (your wedding) next!"), dismissal (**Άντε από 'δω!** "Get out of here!").

check.q: Έλα! on the phone with a friend means:
check.why: Έλα as a greeting on the phone.

sections.title: Vocative particles: βρε, ρε, μωρέ, καλέ

body.p: These particles come before a name or a vocative, or stand alone, and set the emotional tone. They are informal: use them only with people you are on familiar terms with.

head: Particle
Tone
Example
rows: Βρε Νίκο, πού ήσουν; / Βρε, τι λες!
gentle, often used by women, old-fashioned

ex.en: Oh, forget it, it doesn't matter.

body.tip: **Ρε** with a stranger or in a formal setting is rude. **Ρε** + insult is aggressive. With friends it's warm. Listen before you use it.

body.p: **Μωρή** is a feminine vocative particle, rough and often rude (**Μωρή, τι κάνεις εκεί;**). Avoid it unless with very close friends in jest.

check.q: Which particle is safest with an older neighbour you know well?
check.why: Βρε is familiar but less rough than ρε. (With someone older, even βρε needs real familiarity.)

sections.title: Question and doubt particles: μήπως, άραγε, τάχα, δήθεν

head: Particle
Meaning
Example
rows: perhaps, by any chance (softens questions); lest
Μήπως έχεις ένα στιλό; Do you happen to have a pen?
Πού να είναι άραγε; I wonder where it is.
Έκανε τάχα πως δεν με είδε. He pretended not to see me.
Πού να ξέρω; How should I know?

ex.en: Have you seen my keys, by any chance?

body.p: **Μήπως** in statements of fear: **Φοβάμαι μήπως βρέξει** "I'm afraid it might rain". As a polite offer: **Μήπως θέλετε κάτι να πιείτε;** "Would you like something to drink?"

sections.title: Emphatic particles: δα, ντε, μα, κιόλας, πια

head: Particle
Function
Example
rows: Τόσο δα μικρό! This tiny! / Όχι δα! Oh, come on!
Έλα ντε! Come on, then! / Πες το ντε! Say it, then!
Μα τον Θεό! By God! / Μα τι λες; But what are you saying?
already; even, on top of that
Έφυγε κιόλας; Already gone? / Είναι και ακριβό κιόλας. It's expensive too, on top of that.
Δηλαδή δεν έρχεσαι; So you're not coming?
Λοιπόν, πάμε; So, shall we go?
Θα έρθεις, έτσι; You'll come, right?

ex.en: But where were you all this time?
Didn't see that coming, did you?

body.p: **Μα** in oaths: **Μα την Παναγία!** "By the Virgin!", **μα τον Θεό** "by God", **μα την αλήθεια** "honestly". **Μα** "but" is more emotional than αλλά.

sections.title: που and μη in special uses

body.p: **Που** as an exclamation or emphatic particle:

**Μη(ν)** as a question or fear marker: **Μην είναι ο Νίκος;** "Could it be Nikos?"; **Μη(ν) τυχόν και...** "in case, don't you dare": **Μην τυχόν και του το πεις!** "Don't you dare tell him!"; **Μη χειρότερα!** "Heaven forbid worse!"
**Ούτε** as an emphatic particle: **Ούτε λέξη!** "Not a word!", **Ούτε καν** "not even": **Δεν με κοίταξε ούτε καν** "(S)he didn't even look at me".

sections.title: Learned particles: μεν, δε, δη, ου, μη

body.p: Formal Greek keeps a few particles from Ancient Greek:

head: Particle
Function
Example
rows: "on the one hand ... on the other", contrast
Οι μεν δέχτηκαν, οι δε αρνήθηκαν. Some accepted, others refused.
Ο πρόεδρος δε δήλωσε... The president, for his part, stated...
και δη especially: η Ελλάδα, και δη η Αθήνα
ουκ ολίγοι not a few (= many), ουδόλως not at all, ουχί no (formal)
μη κυβερνητική οργάνωση NGO, μη καπνιστής non-smoker

ex.el: Τα μεν αποτελέσματα ήταν θετικά, η δε εφαρμογή προβληματική.
ex.en: The results were positive, but the implementation problematic.

ex.el: Πολλές χώρες, και δη οι μικρότερες, επλήγησαν.
ex.en: Many countries, and especially the smaller ones, were hit.

body.p: **Μη** before adjectives and nouns makes negative compounds in formal style: **μη αναστρέψιμος** irreversible, **μη επανδρωμένο αεροσκάφος** drone, **μη τηρήσεις** non-compliance, **οι μη έχοντες** the have-nots.

check.why: A litotes: "not a few", i.e. many.

title: Particles
blurb: θα, να, ας, δεν, μην, the pointing να, βρε and ρε, and the small discourse words (δα, ντε, μωρέ, μήπως, άραγε) that give spoken Greek its tone.

intro.p: Particles (**μόρια**) are short, unchanging words that do grammatical or expressive work but are not adverbs, conjunctions or interjections in the usual sense. Greek grammar recognises several kinds:

list: **verbal particles** that build the future, the subjunctive and commands: **θα, να, ας**
**affirmative and question particles**: **ναι, μάλιστα, μήπως, άραγε**
the **pointing particle** **να** ("there is!") and the **hortatory** **για** ("come on")
**vocative and emphatic particles** of speech: **βρε, ρε, μωρέ, καλέ, δα, ντε, μα**

intro.p: The first group is pure grammar and you need it from day one. The last group carries tone, emotion and social nuance: it is what makes spoken Greek sound like Greek.
